# Closing-record documentation and core-fit audit

Reviewer: `final_docs`. Scope: independently refute documentation, truthful evidence, action projection, and core fit in the record-only closure. This is not a new runtime review or a hosted-CI certification.

| Layer | Exact reviewed closing revision | Previous independently reviewed code revision | Records/documentation verdict | Independent core-fit verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower | `a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5` | `5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42` | **APPROVE** | **APPROVE** |
| Upper | `87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd` | `4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41` | **APPROVE** | **APPROVE** |

No reproducible closing-record correctness mismatch was found. The closing requirements pass within this lens. These approvals do not claim that the closing revisions have already passed hosted checks or been published; the parent owns those remaining delivery checks.

I used only the mechanical closing inputs, their revision manifest, the two supplied clones and their Git objects, applicable contracts, and my own prior evidence. I did not use other closing verdicts or worker narratives. Historical review JSON was checked as captured data, not accepted as authority for my conclusion.

**What the independent checks establish.** Git tree comparisons include file modes and object identities. Both closing revisions retain **99/99** runtime, test, template, skill, handbook, service, workflow, and contract entries unchanged against their respective code pins. The set includes every scoped `AGENTS.md`, root README and Git attribute/ignore files. Both named code pins and main `326d8ed5fa4f89eaa1402a54d8377dba5946be12` remain ancestors. Thus this closure does not reopen the actual-template runtime verdict or relax the documented R-prefix/apostrophe limitation approved in my r4 report.

Each layer preserves **20/20** existing Markdown files under `message-queue/needs-human/`: 17 question files and three README files. Their existing answers, frozen question bodies, timing, and skill-review binding bytes are unchanged. Exactly one human question is added. Both preserve **41/41** ADR files and **283/283** task files already under main's `4_done/`. Prior history entries are **120/120** unchanged in lower and **121/121** unchanged in upper. Lower adds no handover; upper adds one new handover without changing an old one. The original request moves byte-for-byte with its task in both layers.

The two lower task moves and four combined upper task moves go from `1_in-progress` to `3_in-review`, not `4_done`. The changed design and plan inputs describe the delivered code milestone, retained original histories, and the separate external-review limitation. Exact record-range reconciliation validates task structure/admission, frozen queue history, links, and the new handover under the existing rules without a blocking finding. I found no claim that these open PRs were merged to main.

**Source evidence and action ownership.** The new question names `operation:external-recovery-code-review`, remains `waiting`, and has a blank answer. Its full context and resolution-evidence fields name `memory/facts/external-recovery-review-remains-unexecuted.md`, which does not depend on a task-status folder. Its one decisive quotation is an exact match to the fact's `Execution refusal` section; the separate attribution line is not part of that quotation. The fact and question are identical Git entries in both layers. The upper source checker returns no source problems for the actual question on both interpreters. The lower runtime does not expose that checker; its identical question/source bytes were checked directly and by the upper implementation rather than falsely reporting a lower source-check execution.

The question uses **488 words before the answer**, within the unchanged 800-word budget. It explicitly limits the proposed payload, distinguishes the code review from permission to merge, and says no transmission occurs without an answer. Its timing holds only that unapproved external operation; it does not introduce a human-answer hold on Git publication or the recovery tasks. The fact's Action/Why/If projection is exact in both layers. The upper handover contains **16/16** required unanswered-human entries with exact action labels and copied context, omits the two held/resolved entries, and has `Next steps: None.`. The record-range check also validates the handover against its committed creation snapshot and existing immutability contract.

**Truthful completion and historical evidence.** Both verification records label Claude as **DID NOT RUN**, state that the rejected launcher sent no code, and make no Claude verdict claim. The stable fact records the security refusal; the task's review-limit file is only a pointer and expressly grants no permission. I verified internal consistency and source attribution, not the external service or original launcher history independently.

The publication snapshot identifies lower code `5a9…` and upper code `4008…`, with four recorded successful checks per code candidate. The surrounding prose explicitly says subsequent record-only revisions are checked and published separately. It also distinguishes the parent's five native approvals from GitHub review results. I treated these as historical records, not a new fetch of CI truth. The full-suite records state 16/16 files, name the five ordinary intentional skips, explain the separate corpus/projection runs, and retain the macOS filename limitation. They do not turn an empty record-only test selection into runtime evidence. Localized rollback controls are described as localized controls, not pristine historical-tree runs.

All captured content hashes are internally valid: **5/5** captures in lower and **10/10** in upper. My own captured text is byte-identical to the original report: **1/1** lower and **2/2** upper captures. I cannot independently authenticate the other reviewers' original files from a self-contained hash alone and did not rely on their verdicts. The lower summary accurately preserves my lower template/budget/targeted evidence; it explicitly warns that an older upper discussion in a lower report does not approve the final upper code. My final upper capture retains the exact `4008…` pin, tested R-prefix caveat, counts, and limits.

Regression-map consistency was checked without re-running those tests. Lower's **29/29** named initial methods exist, its 29 green and 29 failing-control rows have consistent result/skip/error fields, and both later portability methods exist. Upper's **74/74** methods exist, all 74 recorded green rows per interpreter and 74 failing-control rows are internally consistent, and its recorded test/runtime blob IDs match the actual closing tree. Those are record-validation counts, not newly observed runtime passes.

**Independent core-fit judgment.** The closure adds no harness mechanism or provider dependency. The existing portable queue/source mechanisms and contracts are unchanged. The new Unicode lesson describes a cross-runtime consistency concern. The Claude-specific fact and authorization question record one bounded disclosure decision; they do not install a provider workflow, alter user-global setup, or grant an external integration access. The revised task rationale still concerns agent/provider/adopter-independent queue integrity. I therefore approve core fit for both exact closing pins independently of the historical captured approvals. The deterministic core-range commands correctly report `no core changes`; that no-op result is not substituted for this judgment or called a revision-bound review receipt.

**Actual selected and executed checks.** Environment: Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, Git 2.55.0. `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` resolves to Python 3.14.6; `/usr/bin/python3` resolves to the Xcode Python 3.9.6. Python 3.9 startup printed Xcode filesystem/cache warnings, but both audit commands exited zero.

| Check performed in this closing audit | Lower | Upper | Skips/qualification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Selected direct record functions, Python 3.14.6 | 12/12 executed, no findings | 12/12 executed, no findings | 0 |
| Same selected functions, Python 3.9.6 | 12/12 executed, no findings | 12/12 executed, no findings | 0 |
| Exact record-range reconciler CLI, Python 3.14.6 | 1/1, exit 0 | 1/1, exit 0 | Lower 5 existing advisories; upper 6 existing advisories |
| Exact record-range core CLI, Python 3.14.6 | 1/1, exit 0 | 1/1, exit 0 | Each reports no core changes |
| Source check of the newly authored question | Not implemented in lower | 1/1 per interpreter, no problems | Lower checked by direct byte equality, not a claimed source-check run |
| Runtime tests/full suites in this audit | 0 selected, 0 executed | 0 selected, 0 executed | Deliberately outside record-only scope |

The 12 direct functions are `check_queue_schema`, `check_queue_name`, `check_queue_location`, `check_human_attention`, `check_fold_shape`, `check_queue_render`, `check_record_swallow`, `check_links`, `check_open_actions`, `check_memory_index`, `check_handover_queue_projection`, and `check_queue_task_reciprocity`. Their overlap with the CLI is not counted as additional distinct coverage. The CLI advisories concern unchanged frozen questions: five wrapped values in two questions on both layers, plus upper's existing aggregate advisory covering nine older question shapes. None identifies the newly authored authorization question. They were not fixed by rewriting frozen files.

Actual validation invocations, with the working directory specified where relevant:

```sh
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=/private/tmp/final-docs-closing-tmp python3 /private/tmp/final-docs-closing-audit.py upper /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-closing 4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41 87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=/private/tmp/final-docs-closing-tmp /usr/bin/python3 -B /private/tmp/final-docs-closing-audit.py lower /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-closing 5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42 a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=/private/tmp/final-docs-closing-tmp /usr/bin/python3 -B /private/tmp/final-docs-closing-audit.py upper /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-closing 4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41 87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd

```

The scripts contain the actual `git --no-replace-objects ls-tree -r -z`, ancestry, HEAD, and status commands used for byte/mode comparisons. I also ran `git diff --name-status -M 4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41 HEAD`, the closing-range `git log`, `git --version`, `uname -srmp`, interpreter version probes, and final `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` in both clones. Both final status outputs were empty.

Complete result logs are `/private/tmp/final-docs-closing-{lower,upper}-audit.log`, `...-{lower,upper}-py39-audit.log`, `...-{lower,upper}-range.log`, `...-{lower,upper}-core.log`, `...-integrity-final.log`, and `...-map.log`. The final integrity helper completed both layers. Two earlier helper attempts failed on my assumptions about string paths and legacy field names; the first also mistakenly included the attribution line in the quotation list. Their scripts and outputs remain preserved as `...-integrity-first-attempt.py`, `...-integrity-second-attempt.py`, `...-integrity.log`, and `...-integrity-corrected.log`. These were reviewer-helper errors, not repository findings or negative runtime controls.

**Limits and process disclosure.** I did not rerun runtime suites, network operations, hosted checks, owner-index preservation, external-provider execution, or original review-control experiments. The parent owns publication, final CI, receipts, shared closing records, and the live owner checkout. No new task, queue item, handover, or repo edit was made by this reviewer. The top-level queue startup and installer were intentionally skipped for this read-only subagent mandate.

Initial help inspection omitted bytecode suppression: three ignored `automation/__pycache__/*.cpython-314.pyc` files are present in each supplied clone (`check_action_projection`, `markdown_semantics`, and `review_receipt`; lower timestamps 02:40:08, upper 02:40:36). This is an incidental filesystem side effect and a deviation from the scratch-only instruction, disclosed to the parent. I did not delete them or claim that the entire filesystem was untouched. Subsequent Python checks used `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. No tracked file, staged content, branch, or Git configuration was changed; all intended artifacts are under the prescribed scratch paths.

The only new pending human action is the already-authored [external-review authorization](/private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-closing/message-queue/needs-human/decisions/blocking-authorize-the-external-recovery-review.md): without an affirmative answer, no code is sent to Claude. It does not block these bounded record/core-fit approvals or authorize that transmission.
